reason: This text (Exodus 3:1-13) presents a narrative of God's call to Moses at the burning bush, featuring God's compassion for the suffering Israelites in Egypt and His commissioning of Moses as deliverer. The passage contains no expression of God's anger (Hebrew אַף, חרה, etc.) toward the people, nor any reference to improper worship practices. While the text mentions future obligation to worship God on the mountain (תַּֽעַבְדוּן֙ אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים), it does not depict God as angry with the people regarding their current worship. The tone is one of divine mercy and initiative, not judgment or anger for worship violations.
